name: Frame Product Strategy
description: Load when an agent must translate user intent and business goals into product priorities, feature decisions, or engagement loops.
scope: Includes problem framing, funnel diagnosis, feature triage, personalization, recommendations, creator ecosystems, gamification, retention, conversion, and consequence analysis; excludes project pricing, visual execution, and detailed screen flows.

name: Scope and Prove Design Work
description: Load when an agent must position, price, present, or demonstrate the value of professional design work.
scope: Includes hourly, fixed, and value-based pricing; client discovery and engagement structure; analytics access; outcome measurement; portfolios, resumes, case studies, and hiring narratives; excludes interface construction and product analytics visualization.

name: Research and Iterate
description: Load when an agent should gather references, diagnose design defects, practise deliberately, or turn critique into an ordered improvement plan.
scope: Includes reference libraries, competitor audits, mood boards, interface replication, low-fidelity testing, self-teaching loops, design audits, iteration workflow, resource selection, and Figma file hygiene; excludes final art direction and specialized usability-flow design.

name: Architect Flows and Navigation
description: Load when an agent must determine what content, screens, branches, navigation, and escape paths a product needs.
scope: Includes information architecture, site maps, screen allocation, onboarding, search, progressive disclosure, empty and error paths, flow coverage, navigation labels, dropdowns, tabs, sheets, modals, and dead-end audits; excludes styling local controls and animating transitions.

name: Adapt Platform Interfaces
description: Load when an agent must make an interface conform to mobile, touch, desktop, or operating-system conventions.
scope: Includes responsive content reduction, mobile navigation, thumb reach, touch targets, gesture models, mobile chrome, bottom sheets, one-handed flows, macOS shells, keyboard-first utilities, drag and drop, and native search patterns; excludes general page composition and motion implementation.

name: Compose Responsive Layouts
description: Load when an agent must organize page-level content into a clear, responsive, conversion-aware spatial hierarchy.
scope: Includes grids, spacing, whitespace, density, focal actions, heroes, landing pages, e-commerce sections, bento grids, carousels, galleries, footers, ruled layouts, cards-in-context, real-viewport validation, and section rhythm; excludes component APIs, palette construction, and brand imagery creation.

name: Build Type Systems
description: Load when an agent must select, measure, scale, pair, space, and apply type for readable interface hierarchy.
scope: Includes typeface classification and licensing, font anatomy, role assignment, modular and fluid scales, line height, tracking, weight, opacity-based hierarchy, display typography, and density-aware sizing; excludes broader colour systems and page copy strategy.

name: Engineer Colour and Depth
description: Load when an agent must create an accessible palette, theme, elevation model, or functional surface treatment.
scope: Includes neutral and accent ramps, OKLCH and HSB derivation, semantic and data colours, interaction-state colours, light and dark themes, contrast, tinted neutrals, surface elevation, borders, shadows, gradients, glass, and image scrims; excludes brand concept development and purely decorative illustration.

name: Build Component Systems
description: Load when an agent must turn recurring interface decisions into consistent tokens, components, variants, and reusable rules.
scope: Includes system scope and governance, spacing and radius tokens, buttons, chips, cards, inputs, tables, tabs, icons, dividers, forms, nav links, component anatomy, variants, consistency audits, and host-product refitting; excludes page-level information architecture and bespoke marketing composition.

name: Design Feedback and Ethical States
description: Load when an agent must specify how controls and interruptions communicate state, outcomes, trust, and user agency.
scope: Includes hover, press, focus, disabled, loading, success, warning and error states; optimistic feedback and rollback; affordances, tooltips, toasts, microcopy, permissions, access gates, dismissals, failure language, humane nudges, and dark-pattern audits; excludes flow topology and animation production.

name: Prototype and Implement Motion
description: Load when an agent must design, prototype, or code motion that explains continuity, state change, hierarchy, or progress.
scope: Includes gesture-linked transitions, easing, springs, staggering, scroll effects, loaders, page transitions, hover and press motion, Figma Smart Animate, masks, matched layers, CSS and GSAP timelines, runtime measurements, fallbacks, and performance restraint; excludes deciding product structure or static visual styling.

name: Design Data Experiences
description: Load when an agent must turn datasets, metrics, or analytical tasks into accurate and decision-oriented interfaces.
scope: Includes dashboard shells and modules, tables, lists, chart selection, axes and legends, categorical colour, density, comparisons, billing and usage views, personal analytics recaps, financial dashboards, data storytelling, and shareable summaries; excludes generic page layout and backend analytics instrumentation.

name: Art-Direct Brand and Imagery
description: Load when an agent must establish a distinctive visual direction or present interface work as a cohesive branded composition.
scope: Includes naming, wordmarks, type-led identity, mood-derived visual systems, photography selection and cropping, illustration, texture, decorative gradients, badges, 3D assets, packaging, product screenshots, mockups, portfolio showcase shots, and presentation treatments; excludes functional UI palette engineering and structural layout decisions.

name: Design AI Product Experiences
description: Load when an agent must design controls, transparency, editing, memory, history, waiting, or trust patterns specific to AI products.
scope: Includes prompt composers, attachments and modes, advanced settings, cost signals, generation history, editable memory, scoped AI edits, selection diffs, reasoning trails, sources, streaming output, skeletons, confidence signals, and AI-product marketing demonstrations; excludes using AI tools to generate the interface itself.

name: Generate and Refine UI with AI
description: Load when an agent must produce an editable interface draft from prompts or references and then bring it to production-quality design standards.
scope: Includes selecting references, constraining prompts, AI UI generation, AI-assisted component sourcing and coding, HTML-to-Figma conversion, targeted Figma cleanup, semantic-state audits, and removal of generator-default layouts, palettes, icons, and decoration; excludes designing AI-product features and general-purpose critique unrelated to generated output.
